subject: Sandbox runway: POC launch & load-day coordination
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@retailx.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@retailx.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff: aligning schedules and load window

Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — RetailX is keen to move to a short POC to validate prompt routing and a small load run with sample traffic. Can we set a kickoff + hands-on session next week where we:
- Introduce stakeholders & map roles
- Walk through prompt templates and routing rules
- Run a 1-hour controlled load test (roughly 50-200 req/min)

Attendees from our side will be me (product), Bala (platform), and our security contact (TBD). Ideal window for us is May 5–7 between 10:00–16:00 PT.

Can you propose a 60–90 minute slot and an agenda? We'll need a short checklist and any artifacts to review ahead of time (routing playbook, expected KV caching behavior, and a runbook for fallback behavior).

Thanks,
Anika
Anika Shah
Product Manager, RetailX

--
Attachment: poc-checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@retailx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: POC kickoff: aligning schedules and load window

Hi Anika — great to hear RetailX is ready to run this. Proposed plan below. Please confirm which day/time in your preferred window works and we'll send a calendar invite.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue May 5, 11:00–12:30 (60–90m)
- Wed May 6, 14:00–15:30
- Thu May 7, 10:30–12:00

Proposed agenda (60–90m):
1) 5m — Introductions & success criteria (stakeholders state goals)
2) 10m — POC scope & acceptance criteria (what counts as pass)
3) 20m — Prompt review: templates, safety tags, and evaluation prompts
4) 15m — Routing & fallback walkthrough (routing rules, model variants)
5) 20m — Hands-on lab: dry run prompts + short validation
6) 20–30m — Load window (controlled burst to target throughput) + monitoring play-by-play
7) 10m — Next steps & deliverables (report, follow-up test plan)

Pre-reads we'll attach: draft-routing-playbook.pdf, poc-checklist.xlsx. For the load test we'll want a named contact at RetailX to kick off the traffic and a point of contact for post-test log collection.

Marissa (CS) — looping you in for success criteria and post-POC acceptance. Dev — can you lead the load runbook and quick notes on tokenization/kv-cache expectations?

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.com

--
Attachments: draft-routing-playbook.pdf (stub), poc-checklist.xlsx (stub)

Date: 2027-05-03T11:22:00-07:00

Thanks — that looks good. A couple of asks from CS:
- Can RetailX confirm a single technical lead who can run the load generator and coordinate logs?
- We'll include a short success-metrics sheet in the pre-read (latency targets, error budget, quality checks).
- Security/compliance: if RetailX wants our security engineer on the kickoff, we'll need to schedule a 20-minute follow-up the same week to go over audit/logging controls.

Dev — can you add a one-paragraph note in the routing playbook about multi-variant fallbacks and token-cost tradeoffs? Also flag any model-quantization we plan to use for the load window.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Anika Shah <anika@retailx.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Bala Kumar <bala.kumar@retailx.com>, platform@retailx.com
Date: 2027-05-04T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: aligning schedules and load window

Ethan / team — thanks, Wed May 6 14:00–15:30 PT works for us.

Confirmed attendees:
- Anika Shah (Product)
- Bala Kumar (Platform lead)
- Priya Menon (Security) — joining for the follow-up security touchpoint (20m)

We'll take the load generator responsibility (Bala will kick off the traffic). I uploaded a quick inventory of sample prompts and traffic profile to the shared Drive folder referenced below.

Please send the invite and the pre-read bundle. Also, one ask: can Redwood include an optional small troubleshooting lab at the end (15m) to exercise fallback scenarios if the first run trips the error budget? That would help our ops team.

Look forward to it — see you on May 6.

Best,
Anika

anika@retailx.com
